thread:
nate: quick sync — I pushed a slot-aware kernel scheduler prototype to the perf branch. saw a weird regression for GQA workloads when seq len jumps between 128->192.

cheng: can you paste the perf numbers? is this before or after the new kv stripe layout change?

nate: after. baseline (master) p50=32ms @ seq=192, new branch p50=38ms. p95 also up. looks like kernel pick is switching to paged-attn_blk128 but the memory layout causes extra bank conflicts.

maya: hmm. we changed KV cache stripe layout last week to improve parallelism on MQA, maybe the paged-attn kernel expects contiguous KV chunks.

alex: do we have repro script? I can run a microbench on A100 vs 80GB V100 to see arch-specific behavior.

nate: repro runnable locally — small harness in tools/bench/slot-scheduler.sh. basically runs mixed MQA/GQA traffic with seq histogram [16:0.3, 64:0.4, 192:0.3].

nate: quick config snippet we used:
```yaml
auto_tune:
  mode: slot-aware
  seq_breakpoints: [64, 128, 256]
  kernels:
    - name: fused_qk_v3
      arch: ampere
      max_seq: 128
    - name: paged_attn_blk128
      arch: ampere
      requires_contig_kv: true
      prefetch: true
```

cheng: that `requires_contig_kv: true` is interesting — our kvstripe layout deliberately interleaves blocks across banks for MQA. if paged_attn assumes contiguous strides it's going to thrash.

maya: could change scheduler to prefer `fused_qk_v3` up to 192 on ampere if kv layout != contiguous. but that may hurt MQA throughput for other seqs. tradeoff.

alex: alternatively add a lightweight kv-layout check in runtime and trigger an on-the-fly layout-compatible kernel or do a one-time relinearize of the KV pages if memory allows. relinearize cost might be amortized for long-lived chats.

nate: tested a quick hack: force `fused_qk_v3` for seq 192 on ampere + stripe layout -> p50 back to 33ms, p95 improved. but we lose ~8% throughput for many small MQA requests.

ci-bot: perf-regression-alert: job=slot-scheduler-e2e, branch=slot-aware, regression detected on seq=192 (p50 +18%). details: https://perf.redwood/internal/slot-aware/1845554321

cheng: thanks CI — can we gate autotuner to only switch kernels when stable (eg, sustained 120s) and not on transient histogram spikes? That would avoid flip-flopping when a single batch has large seqs.

maya: agreed. propose hysteresis: require 3 consecutive windows where new kernel improves p50 by >5% and doesn't regress p95. Also factor in memory-layout-compat flag.

alex: note: on T4 we see different behavior — paged_attn_blk128 wins for seqs >160 even with stripe layout. so scheduler needs arch+layout+seq joint policy.

nate: plan: (1) add layout detection flag to runtime (cheap, one probe per model load), (2) add hysteresis to autotuner, (3) add arch fallback table with explicit kernel prefs. I'll send a PR with tests.

cheng: add a microbenchmark that purposely toggles seq distribution to test hysteresis. also include a stress with mixed MQA channels so we catch bank conflicts.

nate: will do. sample CLI for bench: `./tools/bench/slot-scheduler.sh --model llama-13b --hist "16:30,64:50,192:20" --iters 5000 --kv-layout stripe`

maya: thanks. once PR lands, let's run a dedicated smoke on Dedicated infra (reserved capacity) to ensure no regression in sustained workloads.

alex: I'll run A100/V100/T4 matrix overnight. will post profiler flamegraphs.

nate: sweet. tagging @cheng for kernel selection logic review. :rocket: any objections to landing the gating quickfix today?

cheng: fine with gating fix as short-term. long-term we need a compact policy table.

nate: cool — PR up in ~2h.

ci-bot: build passed for branch slot-aware (linux-amd64). perf tests queued.
